name: Oaxaca
about: The best place in the country to experience Día de los Muertos (Nov 1–2). The Guelaguetza indigenous cultural festival runs two Mondays in late July; rainy season is Jun–Sep, with mild, dry, comfortable weather the rest of the year thanks to the highland elevation.
overview: Mexico's food and mezcal capital, built around a colonial center, indigenous markets, and some of the country's best regional cooking.
costOverview: Street tlayudas, coffee, and local rides are all cheap — a mezcal tasting is the one real splurge most food-focused visits include.

specialSeasons.text: Día de los Muertos (Nov 1–2) fills the city and cemeteries with marigolds, altars and all-night vigils — Oaxaca's single biggest draw.
The Guelaguetza brings dance and music troupes from across Oaxaca's regions for two Mondays of celebration.
